matrix.title: Aging in place
matrix.summary: Goes through the CDC home fall-prevention checklist for the parts the scan can answer, floor by floor: clear paths, steps, stairs, the night path from bed to bathroom, and grab bars.

matrix.title: Amenity census
matrix.summary: Finds and counts a community's amenities in its scans (gym equipment, laundry machines, pool, lounge, business centre, mail room, playground) and sets them beside what the listing claims.

matrix.title: Area profile
matrix.summary: Who lives around a building: population, density, household income, age mix, households, the share renting, rent and home value for its census tract, next to the county.

matrix.title: Bathroom clearance
matrix.summary: Checks each bathroom for a wheelchair: door, turning space, floor space at the toilet and clear of the door, wall for grab bars, and whether the shower has a step.

matrix.title: Camera coverage
matrix.summary: Shows what indoor security cameras would see, which doors, windows and entry paths they cover, and the blind spots; proposes camera spots if you have none.

matrix.title: City census
matrix.summary: Rolls up what has been measured across the city: share of homes a wheelchair can live in by zip code, listed-versus-measured area by property type, smoke alarm coverage by building.

matrix.title: Commute fit
matrix.summary: Estimated drive time from where your people live to each candidate office: the median, who gets a long commute, and transit nearby.

matrix.title: Connectivity
matrix.summary: How well a place is connected: home broadband on offer (fiber, cable, how many providers), bus and rail stops within a walk, the nearest bikeway and the traffic on the nearest counted road. Offered speeds, not measured ones.

matrix.title: Curb to door
matrix.summary: Looks at the way in from outside: parking near the entrance, accessible stalls if the aerial photo shows them, how far it is to the door, and steps at the door.

matrix.title: Daycare capacity
matrix.summary: How many children this space could be licensed for: indoor room area, outdoor play area, toilets and sinks against the Texas or California rule, with the limiting factor named.

matrix.title: Daylight
matrix.summary: Windows, glass area, the way each room faces and its hours of direct sun on a chosen day.

matrix.title: Derived fields
matrix.summary: Proposes the record fields this property lacks, measured from the scan and the aerial photo.

matrix.title: Door widths
matrix.summary: Measures every doorway and flags the ones too narrow for you or what you are moving.

matrix.title: Driveway fit
matrix.summary: Estimates the driveway's length and width from the aerial photo, how many cars park on it, and whether a trailer, RV or boat fits off the street.

matrix.title: Egress routes
matrix.summary: The way out of every room: how far, how narrow, which rooms have one way out, and the hose stretch.

matrix.title: Facility audit
matrix.summary: Your building in one pass: doors, restrooms, ways out, life-safety equipment seen, occupant load and cleaning cost, ending in a prioritised fix list with rough costs.

matrix.title: Ask the facts database
matrix.summary: Answers questions across every scanned building that no fixed tool covers, with the SQL shown.

matrix.title: Feng shui reading
matrix.summary: How a feng shui practitioner would read this home: the front door's direction, the Bagua grid on each floor, the command position for beds and desks, and the usual layout notes. A cultural tradition, not a measured effect.

matrix.title: Field audit
matrix.summary: Across many scans, which record fields disagree with what the scans measure, ranked, with evidence.

matrix.title: Field check
matrix.summary: Lists what the scan could not settle and a person on site can, and records what they found: confirmed, contradicted or measured.

matrix.title: Fire pre-plan
matrix.summary: Writes the pre-incident plan from the scans, the aerial photo and the property record, with a one-page printable sheet.

matrix.title: Flood rehearsal
matrix.summary: Shows what a flood does inside this house: how deep in each room, which doors and windows go under, and the order rooms flood, with the floor-height error carried through.

matrix.title: Floor height
matrix.summary: Narrows the floor's height above the ground, the flood result's widest uncertainty, from steps counted and fixes taken at your own front door.

matrix.title: Furniture fit
matrix.summary: Checks whether a sofa, bed, piano or fridge can be carried from the entrance to a room: each door and turn with its margin, and where it would stick.

matrix.title: Garage fit
matrix.summary: Checks whether your car, truck, van or trailer fits in a scanned garage: how many side by side, the room to open doors, headroom for a lift or roof box, and room for a bench or charger.

matrix.title: Hazard profile
matrix.summary: Every hazard map at an address in one place: FEMA flood zone, hurricane evacuation zone, storm surge, Hurricane Harvey's high-water marks nearby, sea level rise, earthquake faults, liquefaction and landslide zones, fire hazard zones, urban heat, traffic noise, and weather alerts, earthquakes and wildfires now.

matrix.title: Home search for pets and kids
matrix.summary: Finds scanned homes across Houston or Los Angeles that suit your pets or kids: apartments that allow your dog's weight or cats, houses with a fenced, flat yard and no pool, near playgrounds, parks or dog parks.

matrix.title: Industrial fit
matrix.summary: Warehouse check: clear height, dock and drive-in doors, truck court and trailer parking, sprinklers, highway, rail, port and power nearby, and flood zone.

matrix.title: Kids fit
matrix.summary: Whether a home suits young children: stairs that need gates, the pool path with no barrier, windows a child could fall from, a back yard the kitchen looks onto, and the walk to playgrounds, parks and schools.

matrix.title: Smoke alarm census
matrix.summary: Checks every bedroom's ceiling photo for a smoke alarm and lists where none was seen, as leads to check.

matrix.title: Listing claims
matrix.summary: Checks what a listing says against the scan, and lists what it leaves out.

matrix.title: Loading docks
matrix.summary: Counts dock doors and drive-in doors on each wall from the oblique aerial views and beside the CoStar record.

matrix.title: Market comps
matrix.summary: Comparable properties from CoStar: asking rent, sale price per ft², class, year built and space for lease, and where this building sits against them.

matrix.title: Measure search
matrix.summary: Finds homes by what is measured inside them: door widths on the way to the bathroom, turning space, wall lengths, floors, steps. No listing site can search this.

matrix.title: Nearby
matrix.summary: Parks, playgrounds, schools, sports courts and fields, vets, shops and transit near a home, with the walk or ride to the nearest of each along the streets.

matrix.title: Noise level
matrix.summary: How loud each room is, from the phone's microphone: an uncalibrated A-weighted level per room, best read as which rooms are quieter.

matrix.title: Office fit
matrix.summary: Whether your team fits this suite as built: desks, private offices, meeting rooms and kitchen, with the listed size and the last tenant beside it.

matrix.title: Parking count
matrix.summary: Counts parking stalls and parked cars from the aerial photo and compares them with the record.

matrix.title: Path to water
matrix.summary: Traces every route a small child could take from each bedroom to the pool and names the missing barrier.

matrix.title: Permit history
matrix.summary: What was permitted at and near an address, by type and year, and any code enforcement cases (Los Angeles); residents' recent service requests to the city nearby in Houston.

matrix.title: Pet fit
matrix.summary: Whether a home suits your dog, cat or small animal: stairs, floors, a crate and litter spot, a pet door, fall-risk windows, the yard's size, slope, shade and fence, the pool, busy roads, the pet policy and fees, and dog parks and vets nearby.

matrix.title: Photo measure
matrix.summary: Measures a width or a height from one photo that has a bank card, a sheet of paper or a door of known size in it.

matrix.title: Property coverage
matrix.summary: For whoever manages or researches a whole property: which of its floor plans and shared spaces have a scan, and which none covers.

matrix.title: Earthquake readiness
matrix.summary: A safe spot in each room away from windows, tall or heavy furniture near the beds, and where to find the gas shutoff on site.

matrix.title: Quiet rooms
matrix.summary: Ranks the bedrooms and office from quietest to loudest against road, rail and aircraft noise, from the national noise map, the nearest roads and which way each room faces.

matrix.title: Record versus reality
matrix.summary: Sets each fact in the CoStar or listing record beside what the scan and the aerial photo measure, with the evidence.

matrix.title: What if: renovate
matrix.summary: What it would take to make this home wheelchair-ready: the edits, what each one fixes and what it costs, with the renovated plan to compare side by side.

matrix.title: Retail site
matrix.summary: Parking counted from the air and its ratio, the road the site faces, anchors and neighbouring shops, and walk-in proxies.

matrix.title: Risk sheet
matrix.summary: One printable page for an underwriter: roof, flood position, wildfire space, pool, trees and interior hazards, each with its evidence and confidence.

matrix.title: Robot fit
matrix.summary: Shows which rooms a robot of a given width, turning circle and step height can reach and turn in, across one home or many, and which single change to the robot gains the most.

matrix.title: Roof facts
matrix.summary: Roof material, shape, condition, defects, solar, rooftop objects, trees over the roof and height, read from the aerial photo.

matrix.title: Room census
matrix.summary: Which rooms this space has, how big each kind is, and which rooms have no type.

matrix.title: Room labeller
matrix.summary: Names every room of a commercial space from its panoramas, shows what decided each call, and learns from your corrections.

matrix.title: Room sizes
matrix.summary: Every room's floor area, width, depth and ceiling height, biggest first.

matrix.title: Similar rooms
matrix.summary: Finds rooms by what they look like ('a sunlit kitchen with an island'), with measured filters: over 12 m², in Houston, room for a wheelchair to turn.

matrix.title: Site scorecard
matrix.summary: Ranks candidate buildings against your requirements and weights, with a score per criterion, the deal-breakers and the evidence for each cell.

matrix.title: Size-up quiz
matrix.summary: Training: read a house from outside (bedrooms, stairs, kitchen side, floors) and get graded against its measured interior.

matrix.title: Slope check
matrix.summary: Uses the phone as a level: a ramp's slope and cross slope against the ADA limits, a threshold's bevel, or how far a door frame is out of plumb.

matrix.title: Smoke clock
matrix.summary: Minutes of survivable air in each bedroom with its door open and closed, from NIST's fire model run on the measured rooms.

matrix.title: Solar roof
matrix.summary: Usable roof for solar after setbacks and shade, how many panels, kW, kWh a year and payback.

matrix.title: Stairs
matrix.summary: Counts the floors, estimates the steps between the entrance and the bedrooms, and finds steps at doorways, floor by floor.

matrix.title: Step-free route
matrix.summary: Draws the route from the entrance to each room you need, with every door's width, the narrowest point and any step, and says whether you can get there.

matrix.title: Storage space
matrix.summary: Totals closet and storage area and its share of the unit, and finds bedrooms without a closet room.

matrix.title: Storm plan
matrix.summary: An ordered plan for the hours before the storm: what to carry up first, where it goes, plywood cut from your real window sizes, sandbags per door, which shutoffs to turn off, and where a generator can safely stand. It changes when the storm or the household changes.

matrix.title: Stretcher route
matrix.summary: Checks whether a flat ambulance stretcher can be carried from the entrance to each bedroom, and where it would have to be tilted.

matrix.title: Sun by room
matrix.summary: Hours of direct sun in each room on a day and at the solstices and equinoxes, with neighbours and trees in the way, and the best room for plants, a home office and a cool bedroom.

matrix.title: Takeoff bid
matrix.summary: Quantities for a trade from the scan (floor by finish, paintable wall, glass, doors, fixtures), priced with your own rates: a cleaning bid, an apartment unit turn, or a fit-out estimate.

matrix.title: Tour
matrix.summary: Answers by showing: a camera tour from the way in to each piece of evidence the other tools found, with one spoken line at each stop. The last step of a fire pre-plan or a wheelchair check of a home.

matrix.title: Truck access
matrix.summary: Whether a 53 ft trailer can reach and back to the docks: entrance, gate, court depth, turning room, overhead obstructions, arrival directions and a route on the aerial photo.

matrix.title: Turning space
matrix.summary: Finds the largest clear circle in each room and checks it against the turning circle you need.

matrix.title: Unit compare
matrix.summary: Ranks several units or suites side by side on measured area, rooms, storage, windows and door widths, with rent per measured square foot.

matrix.title: What sits below the water
matrix.summary: Finds the belongings, appliances, outlets and utilities in the rooms that flood, how high each sits off the floor, and what the water would cost, as a range.

matrix.title: Walk-through
matrix.summary: A quick safety census of a home with no scan, from a short video you record walking through it: rooms, smoke alarms, hazards and belongings.

matrix.title: Where am I
matrix.summary: Finds the scanned building you are standing in from the phone's GPS, or says there is none here.

matrix.title: Wi-Fi coverage
matrix.summary: Estimates Wi-Fi strength in every room from a router spot, finds dead zones, the best router spot for the bedrooms and office, and where a mesh node helps most.

matrix.title: Wildfire defensible space
matrix.summary: Vegetation and tree canopy in California's 5, 30 and 100 ft zones round the house, what to clear first, roof material, slope, the nearest fire station and the CAL FIRE hazard zone.

matrix.title: Window check
matrix.summary: Point the phone out of a window: its compass confirms or corrects which way the room faces and its hours of sun.

matrix.title: Zoning check
matrix.summary: What the zoning allows on a lot: the zone, its main uses and height or density limits in Los Angeles; in Houston, which has no zoning, the city's lot-size, building-line and historic rules.

features.why: One building or one whole property per subagent, each with its own context, so ten buildings do not crowd one context window.
Buildings are independent, so they are checked at the same time; middleware reports each tool call and the panel shows one lane per subagent.
The plan is the person's progress view, not hidden state.
Case notes per building in state; `/memories/` in the store; `/skills/` read-only from disk.
A second investigation of a building starts from what the last one learned.
Procedures for fire pre-plan, storm prep, step-free home and record check load only when the need matches.
A smoke simulation, a vision read of every panorama, a plan edit or a city rollup waits for "Run it / Skip it / Always run it here".
A paused turn resumes in any server process, even after a restart.
Catches the closing message stating numbers or claiming checks did not run; a real turn made that mistake before this existed.
The read-only MongoDB MCP server's tools, behind a guard, answer counts over the person's own past work.
Every turn is one trace tagged by persona; the composer's briefs are a dataset, and each prompt change is an experiment scored per check.

left_out.why: The person's preferences already go into the prompt, so a static file would repeat it.
They need an Agent Protocol server. Slow tools already run in the background, and subagents run in parallel.
The agent runs no shell. Every action is a typed tool, and a shell would only add risk.
There is one model, so there is nothing to tune per model.

features.feature: Hypertables for facts, flood simulations and the op log
features.why: Facts are measured again as tools improve; the history is time series by nature.
234 MB to 58 MB on the cloud service.

features.feature: Continuous aggregates, real-time, plus a hierarchical one
features.why: The Insights page reads daily rollups that include a fact measured a second ago, and a neighbourhood rollup built on them.
Medians that roll up across days and areas.
Distance filters in search by measurement.

features.feature: pgvector + pgvectorscale StreamingDiskANN with label filters, BM25
features.why: Similar-room search filtered by room type inside the index, blended with words.
Room descriptions embed themselves inside the database when they change (Ollama, nomic-embed-text).
Rebuilds the room-search graphs hourly, because a graph grown row by row had recall@10 of 0.0.
The analytics copy of the op log deletes itself after the event, as CoStar's terms require.

features.feature: Read-only role for the agent's SQL
features.why: The agent can ask its own questions of the facts and cannot write.
City-wide what-if on a zero-copy fork, ready in about 31 s on the free plan, deleted after.

left_out.why: It runs with the service owner's credentials. The agent's own read-only SQL role, with a 5 second timeout, is stricter.

left_out.feature: Tiered storage, read replicas, high availability
left_out.why: Paid or operations features with no use at this size.
No view plots a gap-filled or time-weighted series yet.
The columnstore policies already compress older chunks.

features.feature: Documents with a unique (workspace, seq) index
features.why: An optimistic lock: two writers cannot both append operation n.
A person's operation and what it taught the agent land together.
Live sync between server processes, browsers and the phone: a door width typed on the phone reaches the desktop in about a second.
The append-only log refuses a malformed entry.
Read-only share links delete themselves.
Search past investigations with counts by tool, status and city.

features.feature: Vector Search with filters, automated embedding (voyage-4)
features.why: Recall similar past needs per persona, with no embedding key in the app.
"Could not roll a chair into the toilet" finds "No ADA clearance at the toilet".
Every phone reading (GPS, altitude, tilt, sound) as one measurement; the timeline groups by minute with `$dateTrunc`.
Shortlisted buildings near a point.
Paused agent turns and long-term memory next to the workspaces.
The agent counts and groups over the person's own past work.

left_out.why: They need App Services keys. Change streams already react to inserts inside the server.

left_out.feature: Stream Processing, Online Archive, Data Federation
left_out.why: Paid tiers, and no stream or archive need at a weekend's volume.
No field is more sensitive than the documents as a whole, and it would need a key service.
The app draws its own panels from the result objects.

features.feature: Asks in plain words, gets the floor plan picture marked with findings, the verdict, the measurements and a workspace link
features.why: Shared iMessage line, native replies, attachment upload, typing indicator

features.feature: Replies to an earlier answer ("what about a 76 cm chair?")
features.why: The reply thread is the investigation (`parentMessageId` in and out)

features.feature: Says "yes", "no" or "always" to a slow step
features.why: Approvals by native reply

features.feature: Sends a photo of a doorway with a bank card, a ceiling photo, a short video, a voice note, a location
features.why: Inbound attachments, video, audio and vCard locations each run a tool
Unsettled checks arrive one at a time; each reply settles one and the desktop workspace updates live
The PDF arrives in the chat, ready to forward
Answers also arrive as native iMessage voice messages
The chat background becomes the building's plan; a National Weather Service alert at that building arrives once with their own flood result
An ElevenLabs agent over SIP runs the same checks by voice; the plan and link follow in iMessage after the call (Best Voice Agent)

focus.sees: The agent also decides what not to do from what it knows: skip a question, leave out a tool, keep back checks; each decision is one row under "Because of what Cranley knows about you"
A chair width said once is used on every later home: doorways, step-free route and bathroom door, with "Using your doorway width: 0.7 m" on each result
A profile across investigations, each line with its source, Change and Forget; "Not relevant" hides that kind now and later, "Useful" lists it first
focus.where: "Cranley knows" (agent panel, Home, Settings); Checks tab

focus.sees: No profile form: it fills from answers and clicks the person makes anyway; Home says in one line how much is known
The proof is in the product: "How Cranley has adapted to you" counts what each investigation asked, reused and kept back, from the person's own logs

criteria.serves: An agent that builds the interface per need instead of a chat box; physics and geometry instead of text answers.
The wheelchair, flood, fire, garage, pet and furniture tools answer questions people ask on forums every day. The iPhone scan makes it work on any building.
About 600 server tests and 90 web tests; every tool run on a 15-place demo set with a matrix of results (see Proof); FastAPI, deepagents, two cloud databases, our own 3D renderer and splat training.
The App look: one thing first on every screen, the rest folded; plain-word reliability chips; every panel resizable; guided first run; both themes; phone companion with live sync.

quotes.said: "I don't ask them if it's wheelchair accessible. I ask them if they have any steps." (07:05) Steps are the hard limit: no wheelchair goes over steps "unless you're young, athletic, and use a manual chair" (03:44).
quotes.became: `step_free_route`: the verdict now opens with "Steps from the entrance:" and one answer per destination, and each destination gets a steps check before any width check (`steps.<room>`: the highest sill step measured, against ADA 303's 1/2 in). A step at the entrance door is named as such. Commits 80becdd, 1259b9e

quotes.said: Asked by email and phone, "is it wheelchair accessible? Yes. I get there, and there's a step, and I couldn't go in. I have a 400-pound chair." (05:22) "There's no certification ... we have the ADA ... but there's no police for it." (11:57)
quotes.became: `step_free_route`, `bathroom_clearance`: a "Not in the scan" line says the ADA has no certification or inspection, so "accessible" is the owner's word. 80becdd, 1690b38

quotes.said: "You go in four feet or seven feet or ten feet from the front door. There's a set of steps." At a bookstore: "I could get in the bookstore, but I couldn't go to the books." (05:57)
quotes.became: `step_free_route`: every doorway sill on the route is measured, and a step, stair or ramp the panorama reader sees in a room the route passes through now counts against that route (it turns a pass into "measure on site"), not only as a pin. 80becdd

quotes.said: Lobby steps in NYC apartment buildings: "you could get to the desk, but you can't get to the elevators." (18:58)
quotes.became: Not in the scan (an apartment unit scan starts at the unit door): `step_free_route` says so and points to `curb_to_door`. 80becdd

quotes.said: "A lot of people have more than one chair ... I have a travel chair. I know it's more narrow than my everyday chair." Most people do not know their chair's width. (02:19)
quotes.became: New preference `access.chairs` (each chair: name, door width it needs, turning circle). `step_free_route` routes each chair and lists which rooms each one reaches; `bathroom_clearance` checks each chair at the bathroom door and turning circle; `turning_space` checks each chair's circle. A chair with no size uses the person's default. The profile shows each chair. 80becdd, 87a0f05, 4d36cd6

quotes.said: "If it opens in, you typically cannot get in because the door is blocking." (09:45)
quotes.became: `bathroom_clearance`: a check per bathroom door on which way it opens: from the scan if it records it, else read from the panorama (a label, not a size), else "not in the scan" with low reliability. Opening in with no 30 x 48 in space clear of the swing fails. 1690b38

quotes.said: A big garbage can next to the toilet: "an accessible stall, but it was made inaccessible." (10:08) Clear space in front of versus beside the toilet decides a front or side transfer. (10:30)
quotes.became: `bathroom_clearance`: clear floor in front of the toilet (30 in strip, needs 48 in) and beside it (48 in deep, needs 30 in), measured from the wall behind the toilet, with objects a phone scan measured (bins, storage, vanities) taken out of the floor and named when they are in the way. The toilet's own position comes from the phone scan when it measured one. On wall-graph scans, which record no objects, a line says every clear space is the most there can be. 1690b38

quotes.said: Toilet height and grab bars are the other bathroom checks she makes. (10:30)
quotes.became: Grab bar wall space was already checked. Toilet seat height and whether walls can hold bars are now a "Not in the scan" line. 1690b38

quotes.said: 99 cent stores with one narrow aisle and boxes on the floor, "nowhere to turn around." (22:28)
quotes.became: `turning_space`: on scans with measured objects, the turning circle is fitted to the floor less the objects, and a new aisle check gives the widest body that can get from the doorway to the turning spot between them (against ADA 403.5.1's 36 in). Boxes or stock left out on the day are a "Not in the scan" line. 1baf92b

quotes.said: A bookstore's elevator was out, so she could not reach the graphic novels. (20:29) Disabled In Action sued a pharmacy chain over pharmacies on other floors; it took 17 years to resolve. (27:15)
quotes.became: `step_free_route`: a room on another floor reads "elevator only" when the scan has a room labelled elevator or lift, otherwise "stairs only, no elevator in the scan"; a new check lists the rooms on the entrance floor reached with no step at any doorway, the ones that need a step, and the other floors. Whether the elevator is in service is a "Not in the scan" line. 80becdd

quotes.said: Temporary obstructions: cardboard bales that trapped her, cleaning supplies kept in elevators, accessible fitting rooms used for storage. (28:44)
quotes.became: "Not in the scan" line in `step_free_route` and `turning_space`. 80becdd, 1baf92b

quotes.said: The gap between a subway platform and the train "works like a step." (07:53)
quotes.became: Skipped: the scans are buildings, not transit platforms.

quotes.said: "Worldwide, I'm sure door width would be a huge issue." (21:50)
quotes.became: No change: `door_widths` and `step_free_route` already measure every doorway.

quotes.said: Needs differ by person and over time: after foot surgery she could not walk for three months. (18:20)
quotes.became: No change: every size is an editable preference, so a person can change it.

skipped.said: The gap between a subway platform and the train "works like a step." (07:53)
skipped.why: Skipped: the scans are buildings, not transit platforms.
Skipped: it depends on the equipment layout, which no scan records.

skipped.said: "Don't believe in the first five feet; focused on vegetation type." Pool pump, fire hoses, a generator.
skipped.why: Skipped: plant species are not in the aerial data (the tool reads green and height only), and the equipment is the owner's, not the building's.

skipped.said: A landlord filming influencer content during service; "Experience".
